# Preference is not one score: establish feedback format before choosing an alignment objective

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/post-training/preference-and-alignment.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-27 · 25 topic entries / 6 representative comparisons

DPO, KTO, SimPO, ORPO, and IPO change how feedback is used; CleanRM first asks whether feedback is reliable. References, length normalization, finite margins, and label-noise corrections are independent axes even if all distinguish better from worse responses.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Mechanism comparison {#comparison}

Axes: Supervision unit: same-prompt pairs, individual desirability labels, or noisy labels · Reference and scale: reference log-ratio, length average, and odds · Objective shape: increasing separation, finite margin, or joint SFT and preference · Source of error: excessive optimization pressure versus noisy labels

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Start from observed data, not labels implied by a fashionable loss

DPO, SimPO, ORPO, and IPO use relative outcomes between responses to the same question. KTO can use single-answer feedback. Pairing reactions across questions invents an unobserved comparison. CleanRM instead estimates how noisy labels differ from clean preferences and corrects training risk; swapping the preference objective does not do this.

Sources: [DPO](../../../../post-training/2305.18290-dpo/README-en.md) · [KTO](../../../../post-training/2402.01306-kto/README-en.md) · [CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF](../../../../post-training/2610.21138-clean-rm/README-en.md)

### Reference-free and less overfitting are separate choices

SimPO removes the reference but keeps mean token reward and a fixed margin. ORPO combines SFT and odds preference. IPO keeps the reference and fits a finite gap. Analyze memory, length scaling, chosen-text likelihood, and saturation separately rather than collapsing them to one local accuracy number.

Sources: [SimPO](../../../../post-training/2405.14734-simpo/README-en.md) · [ORPO](../../../../post-training/2403.07691-orpo/README-en.md) · [IPO](../../../../post-training/2310.12036-ipo/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Should individual thumbs-up/down feedback be forced into DPO pairs or handled with KTO? {#cross-binary-feedback-versus-pair}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Preserve the observed feedback unit. DPO needs a same-prompt comparison; KTO uses individual desirability and a KL reference. Reactions across prompts do not form a preference pair. Collect or reliably construct real same-prompt comparisons before choosing a pairwise loss.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: A thumbs-up on question A and thumbs-down on question B do not say which two answers to A are preferred.

    Sources: [DPO](../../../../post-training/2305.18290-dpo/README-en.md) · [KTO](../../../../post-training/2402.01306-kto/README-en.md)

### Can SimPO and ORPO be interchanged by turning off DPO's reference? {#cross-reference-free-two-objectives}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. SimPO compares length-averaged policy log-probabilities against a fixed margin. ORPO also improves chosen likelihood and compares odds. Removing a reference does not supply either definition or equalize length and probability bounds.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: ORPO's chosen NLL independently contributes gradients even when preference separation increases; it is not a SimPO margin.

    Sources: [SimPO](../../../../post-training/2405.14734-simpo/README-en.md) · [ORPO](../../../../post-training/2403.07691-orpo/README-en.md) · [DPO](../../../../post-training/2305.18290-dpo/README-en.md)

### Can a finite IPO margin fix a correct answer mislabeled rejected? {#cross-finite-margin-versus-label-cleaning}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not automatically. IPO bounds the target gap but still uses the supplied direction. CleanRM instead estimates noise and corrects risk, contingent on estimator quality. Reduced pressure does not clean labels.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Making the actually better answer lose by a smaller amount still does not reverse the wrong label.

    Sources: [DPO](../../../../post-training/2305.18290-dpo/README-en.md) · [IPO](../../../../post-training/2310.12036-ipo/README-en.md) · [CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF](../../../../post-training/2610.21138-clean-rm/README-en.md)
